metadata.title: Exposition of the Mass, Part II
metadata.author: Florus of Lyon
known_issues: Several printed biblical references in this chunk appear to be confused or impossible in standard modern numbering; they have been rendered aloud exactly as printed and explained in the relevant notes.
The printed “in omnibus nis” in the Daniel quotation is corrupt; translated according to the evident sense, “in all these things.”
The printed citation “II Joan. I, 7” is erroneous for the quoted text, which is from First John 1:7; it was nevertheless spoken as printed.
The Latin word “puer” can mean either “child” or “servant”; the translation makes this explicit where Florus comments on Abel and David.
The printed citation Genesis chapter twenty-two, verse twelve contains wording that extends beyond that verse in the biblical text, but it was rendered as printed.
The phrase “testamentis suis” in the Ambrose quotation is difficult; translated contextually as “his own devices.”
The final section depends on Florus’s etymological explanation of 'missa' as dismissal or sending away, so the Latin term is retained where he discusses it directly.
Editorial column markers from the source have been omitted from the English, as they are not part of Florus’s text.

The phrase “sed non praeceduntur ab Ecclesia” in section 68 is difficult; the translation gives the apparent theological sense, that the faithful dead go before the living but remain within the Church.
The printed citation “II Cor. V, 5” appears to point to verse five, while the quoted wording corresponds chiefly to 2 Corinthians 5:1; it was spoken as printed.
The printed citation Hebrews chapter six, verse three appears to correspond to Hebrews chapter seven, verses two through three, but it was rendered as printed.
The phrase “in condensis” is unusual; translated conservatively as “in dense assemblies.”
The printed Latin includes readings that differ from the standard Vulgate text, especially Hebrews 13:20 and Zechariah 9:10; these have been translated as printed unless otherwise noted.
The printed text contains a few apparent scribal or typographical forms, noted in the relevant chunks, such as “clamanus” for “clamamus” and “suppliter” for “suppliciter.”
The printed citation to the letter to the Hebrews gives only chapter five, verse one, though the quotation continues into the following verses.

Several Psalm and New Testament citations are spoken exactly as printed even where the quoted wording extends beyond, or differs from, the printed verse reference; details are noted in the relevant chunks.
The Daniel citation is spoken as printed even though the combined quotation appears to draw on more than Daniel chapter nine, verse twenty-three.

The printed references to the Gospel of John, chapter six, verses fifty-nine and fifty-seven do not align with many modern verse numberings; they have been spoken as printed and noted in the relevant chunks.
The Latin punctuation around Gregory’s quotation in section seventy-two is not fully explicit; the translation follows the evident transition in sense.
In chunk 18, “in corde suo” is unusual; it has been translated as printed rather than emended.
The Zechariah citation is spoken as printed, though the quoted passage aligns with Zechariah chapter one, verse twelve in common Vulgate numbering.
The printed citation “Ibid., 33” in section fifty-three is likely erroneous; it has been spoken as printed and explained in the note.
Several liturgical quotations are abbreviated with “etc.” in the Latin; they have not been completed from memory, in accordance with the work-specific instructions.
Several biblical quotations in this passage have no printed references in the Latin; no references were added in the English.
The printed citation “IV Reg. XXXI, 6” in section fifty-seven is impossible as a biblical location; it has been spoken as printed and explained in the note.

The printed citation to the Gospel of John, chapter one, verse three, reflects a punctuation and verse-boundary issue; the wording corresponds to material now usually read across verses three and four.

Several biblical quotations are cited according to the printed references even where the wording extends beyond, or does not exactly match, the cited verse; discrepancies are noted without altering the printed citation.
The printed citation Matthew chapter twenty-two, verse thirty-five appears to correspond to Matthew chapter twenty-three, verse thirty-five, but it was rendered as printed.
Some biblical citations in the printed Latin appear to use verse numbering that differs from modern or standard Vulgate numbering; they have been spoken as printed and noted locally.

Several printed biblical citations do not match the usual verse numbering or the exact source of the quotation; each citation has been spoken as printed, with discrepancies recorded in the relevant notes.
Several biblical quotations in the Latin are introduced without explicit printed references; no new references were added in the English.
Some biblical quotations in the Latin are given without printed references; these were not supplied in the English except where the Latin itself printed a citation.
In chunk 17, “(Ibid., l b. X, cap. 19.)” is treated as an Augustine source siglum based on the preceding context; the printed abbreviation is irregular.

corrections.original: : The Canon Begins with Humble Supplication
corrections.latin: DE EXPOSITIONE MISSAE
corrections.reason: The spoken heading carries a chapter subtitle that is not in the Latin heading; the subtitle stays in chapter_title. Matches Part I, whose chunk 1 English is 'Exposition of the Mass' alone.

corrections.original: not merely with his voice, but with his heart
corrections.corrected: not with his voice, but with his heart
corrections.latin: clamat sacerdos cum Ecclesia non voce, sed corde dicens
corrections.reason: 'merely' is added; Florus's plain 'not with the voice but with the heart' points to the canon said silently, and 'not merely' reverses the point.

corrections.original: not simply the body lying prostrate, but
corrections.corrected: not the prostration of the body, but
corrections.latin: In qua flexione genuum non corporis prostratio, sed supplex affectus
corrections.reason: 'simply' softens the Latin's plain contrast (non ... sed).

corrections.original: toward us, sinners and unworthy servants, has been
corrections.corrected: toward us, sinners and unworthy as we are, has been
corrections.latin: cujus erga nos peccatores et indignos
corrections.reason: 'servants' is added; the Latin has no noun here.

corrections.original: by being praised, it is commended to God.
corrections.corrected: by being praised, it is commended.
corrections.latin: diversa appellatione laudatur, et laudando commendatur
corrections.reason: 'to God' is added; 'commendatur' means the reality is commended (held up for honor), as the same phrase is rendered in §64.

corrections.original: “If you offer your gift at the altar.”
corrections.corrected: “If you are presenting your offering at the altar.”
corrections.latin: et «munera» appellantur, sicut Dominus in Evangelio dicit: «Si offers munus tuum ad altare»
corrections.reason: The proof-text is cited for the word 'munera' (rendered 'offerings'); rendering 'munus' as 'gift' loses the point for a listener, and 'gifts' is used for 'dona' in the next sentence.

corrections.original: The printed section number “46” and column markers are editorial and are not voiced in the English. Marginal siglum recorded as printed: “(ISID. lib. VIII Origin., c. 1.)”. In the English, per instruction, it is rendered only as “[Isidore].” The citation to Paul’s first letter to Timothy, chapter two, verse one, is spoken as printed, though the final quoted clause corresponds to the following verse in the usual division. The printed citation Psalm one hundred thirty-one, verse one is spoken as printed, though the quoted “Behold how good…” is commonly numbered Psalm one hundred thirty-two, verse one in many modern Bibles. The printed citation Psalm twenty-seven, verse eight is spoken as printed; the quoted wording is commonly associated with the following verse in the Vulgate tradition and with Psalm twenty-eight in many modern numberings.
corrections.corrected: Printed 'id idipsum custodire quod et regere' is an evident misprint for 'et idipsum'; translated by the evident sense ('and to guard seems to mean the same thing as to govern').
corrections.latin: id idipsum custodire
corrections.reason: record evident misprint read by sense

corrections.original: not among the other things we say beforehand, by which we open the way, in the mysteries, for the prayers that are to follow.
corrections.corrected: not among the other things we say beforehand—so that by the mysteries themselves we may open the way for the prayers that are to follow.
corrections.latin: ut inter sacra mysteria nominentur, non inter alia quae ante praemittimus, ut ipsi mysteriis viam futuris precibus aperiamus
corrections.reason: The purpose clause belongs to the main point (names are read within the mysteries); the English made it a relative clause about the preliminary prayers. 'ipsi' is read as 'ipsis' (see note).

corrections.original: The printed Latin has “[cum] fidem,” an editorial insertion; the translation renders the evident sense, “this faith and devotion.” The phrase “Tu enim solus nosti corda filiorum hominum” echoes First Kings chapter eight, verse thirty-nine in the Vulgate tradition, but no citation is printed in the source, so none is added in the translation.
corrections.corrected: In the Innocent quotation the printed text is corrupt at two places, translated by the evident sense: 'ne tunc eorum nomina … edicenda' is read as 'ac tunc' ('and only then should the names … be announced'), and 'ut ipsi mysteriis' as 'ipsis mysteriis' ('by the mysteries themselves').
corrections.latin: ne tunc eorum nomina … ut ipsi mysteriis
corrections.reason: record corrupt readings handled by evident sense

corrections.original: the blood of my offering upon leaven
corrections.corrected: the blood of my victim upon leaven
corrections.latin: Non immolabit super fermento sanguinem hostiae meae
corrections.reason: 'offering' is reserved for oblatio (glossary); hostia is rendered 'victim' elsewhere in this part (§§64–65).

corrections.original: is a victim, an offering, and a sacrifice
corrections.corrected: is a victim, a sacrificial offering, and a sacrifice
corrections.latin: eadem lex et victimam et hostiam et sacrificium esse commendat
corrections.reason: Keeps 'offering' (oblatio) distinct from hostia while preserving the threefold list.

corrections.original: “No one who is unclean in his soul,
corrections.corrected: “Anyone who is unclean in his soul,
corrections.latin: «Nemo,» inquit, «qui fuerit immundus super anima sua, in via procul in gente vestra, faciat phase Domino mense secundo» (Num. IX, 10)
corrections.reason: Printed 'Nemo' reverses the sense: Numbers 9:10 (Vulgate 'homo') allows the unclean and the traveller to keep the Passover in the second month, and Florus's next quotation (9:13, the clean man who fails to keep it is cut off) presupposes that sense. Owner rule: translate the evident sense and note it.

corrections.original: The phrase “offerre spiritales hostias et acceptabiles Deo per Jesum Christum” is printed after the citation to First Peter chapter two, verse nine, but corresponds to First Peter chapter two, verse five; the translation keeps the wording where Florus places it and speaks only the printed citation. “Quod vobis immolatus est Christus” is syntactically awkward in the printed Latin; the translation renders the evident Pauline sense, “which is Christ, sacrificed for you,” echoing First Corinthians chapter five, verse seven, but no citation is printed there.
corrections.corrected: The printed Latin reads 'Nemo … faciat phase Domino mense secundo' ('No one … shall keep the Passover in the second month'), which reverses Numbers 9:10 (Vulgate 'homo'); the English gives the evident sense, 'Anyone who is unclean … shall keep the Passover to the Lord in the second month.'
corrections.latin: «Nemo,» inquit, «qui fuerit immundus
corrections.reason: record evident misprint translated by sense

corrections.original: This is cited as the same psalm, verse thirty-three.
corrections.corrected: This is cited as Psalm forty-nine, verse thirty-three.
corrections.latin: (Ibid., 33)
corrections.reason: 'Ibid.' is spelled out elsewhere in this part (§59); a chunk heard on its own gives 'the same psalm' no referent. The note already identifies Psalm 49.

corrections.original: Printed siglum: “(AUG., serm. 186).” The Latin “Genitrix Dei” and “Dei genitrix” are translated as “Mother of God,” preserving the Christological sense of Theotokos without introducing Greek into the narration.
corrections.corrected: Printed 'cum que falso' is read as 'cumque falso' (a word-division misprint); translated by the evident sense.
corrections.latin: cum que falso
corrections.reason: record evident misprint read by sense

corrections.original: because they themselves belong to it.
corrections.corrected: because they themselves are also this sacrifice.
corrections.latin: quod non offertur ipsis, quia hoc sunt et ipsi
corrections.reason: Augustine identifies the saints with the sacrifice ('hoc sunt et ipsi'); 'belong to it' weakens the identification.

corrections.original: Printed sigla: “(VIGILIUS.)” and “(AUG., de Civ. Dei, l. XXII, c. 10.)”. The printed citation “(IV Reg. XXXI, 6)” is rendered as printed. It appears corrupt: Fourth Kings has no chapter thirty-one, and the quotation corresponds to Fourth Kings, chapter nineteen, verse thirty-four in the Vulgate, equivalent to Second Kings, chapter nineteen, verse thirty-four in many modern Bibles.
corrections.corrected: Printed 'altaria inquibus' is a word-division misprint for 'in quibus'.
corrections.latin: altaria inquibus
corrections.reason: record trivial misprint

corrections.original: Printed source siglum “(AUG., lib. XX contra Faust, c. 13.)” rendered as [Augustine]. Editorial column markers are omitted from the English. The printed “(Ibid., LVIII)” is rendered self-contained as “the Gospel of John, chapter six, verse fifty-eight,” because it refers back to the preceding citation of John chapter six. The phrase “in corde suo” is translated as printed, “in his own heart”; the wording is unusual in context and may reflect a textual difficulty, but no emendation has been made.
corrections.corrected: 'juxta Apostolum fidelem praecipientem' is translated as printed ('the faithful Apostle's command'); 'fidelem' may be a misprint for 'fideles' ('the Apostle instructing the faithful'), but this is uncertain and the English is unchanged.
corrections.latin: juxta Apostolum fidelem praecipientem
corrections.reason: record uncertain reading

corrections.original: How much more will the blood of Christ, who through the Holy Spirit offered himself without blemish to God, cleanse our conscience
corrections.corrected: How much more has the blood of Christ, who through the Holy Spirit offered himself without blemish to God, cleansed our conscience
corrections.latin: Quanto magis sanguis Christi … emundavit conscientiam nostram
corrections.reason: The printed text has the perfect 'emundavit' (Florus then glosses 'emundavit, id est innovavit'); the future followed the familiar Vulgate wording, which the printed text lacks.

corrections.original: bound by hope of the redemption still to come
corrections.corrected: held bound in hope of the redemption still to come
corrections.latin: et antiqui justi spe futurae redemptionis devincti ab inferni claustris educti sunt
corrections.reason: The righteous of old were held bound (in the prison of the underworld, cf. 'vinctos tuos de lacu'); hope is their state, not what binds them.

corrections.original: which is repeated in that offering
corrections.corrected: which is celebrated again and again in that offering
corrections.latin: sacramentum Dominicae passionis et mortis, quod illa oblatione frequentatur
corrections.reason: 'frequentatur' = celebrated often; 'repeated' can be heard as the passion itself being repeated.

corrections.original: because, while we were still sinners, Christ died for us. Much more,
corrections.corrected: because, if Christ died for us while we were still sinners, much more,
corrections.latin: quoniam si, cum adhuc peccatores essemus, Christus pro nobis mortuus est, multo magis
corrections.reason: The printed text has the conditional 'si'; the English followed the familiar Vulgate wording, which the printed text lacks.

corrections.original: Printed source siglum: (GREG.). The reference printed as Romans 8:9–10 is spoken as given, though the quoted material corresponds to Romans 5:8–10.
corrections.corrected: Printed 'ut transeat a hoc mundo' is an evident misprint for 'ab hoc' (Vulgate 'ex hoc'); translated 'to pass from this world'.
corrections.latin: ut transeat a hoc mundo
corrections.reason: record evident misprint read by sense

corrections.original: the innocence of grace, praising God, is placed before the earthly works of the Old Testament
corrections.corrected: that faith which, praising God in the innocence of grace, is placed before the earthly works of the Old Testament
corrections.latin: Novi Testamenti fides praefigurabatur, qua innocentia gratiae Deum laudans, Veteris Testamenti terreni operibus anteponitur
corrections.reason: The subject of 'anteponitur' is the faith ('qua' = quae fides); 'innocentia' is ablative.

corrections.original: The parenthetical reference “(In psal. XLII, n. 5)” is an editorial patristic source reference and is not spoken as a Bible citation. The quotation “Et introibo ad altare Dei…” comes from Psalm forty-two in the Vulgate, but no scriptural reference is printed at that point, so none is added in the English.
corrections.corrected: 'Dies … solemnis est Domino conjunctio cordis nostri' is translated as printed ('the joining of our heart'); the following clause on tears and lamentation suggests that 'conjunctio' may be a misprint for 'compunctio' ('compunction of our heart'), Gregory's usual term, but this is uncertain and the English is unchanged.
corrections.latin: Dies, inquit, solemnis est Domino conjunctio cordis nostri
corrections.reason: record uncertain reading

corrections.original: the most holy body and blood of your Son,
corrections.corrected: the most holy body and blood of the Son,
corrections.latin: sacrosanctum Filii corpus et sanguinem sumpserimus
corrections.reason: The printed lemma has 'Filii' without 'tui'; 'your' supplied the canon from memory.

corrections.original: by sharing in so great a Lord
corrections.corrected: by so great a sharing in the Lord
corrections.latin: ut, tanta Domini participatione, intra se Deum suscipientes
corrections.reason: 'tanta' agrees with 'participatione', not with 'Domini'.

corrections.original: the place is closed to his own devices.
corrections.corrected: the place is closed to his temptations.
corrections.latin: locum testamentis suis interclusum esse per Christum
corrections.reason: Printed 'testamentis' is evidently a misprint for 'tentamentis' (temptations, assaults); 'his own devices' was a guess at the sense without naming the misprint.

corrections.original: “testamentis suis” is rendered “his own devices”; the wording is somewhat difficult, but the sense is that the enemy finds no place in the soul occupied by Christ.
corrections.corrected: Printed “testamentis suis” is an evident misprint for “tentamentis suis” and is translated “his temptations”: the enemy finds no place for his assaults in the soul occupied by Christ.
corrections.latin: locum testamentis suis interclusum
corrections.reason: name the misprint and replace the superseded note

corrections.original: as far as, “we pray that you grant them a place of refreshment, light, and peace.”
corrections.corrected: as far as, “of light and peace, we pray that you grant.”
corrections.latin: etc., usque «lucis et pacis indulgeas deprecamur.»
corrections.reason: The 'usque' lemma gives only 'lucis et pacis indulgeas deprecamur'; 'them a place of refreshment' completed the prayer from memory (owner rule B).

corrections.original: Yet they have not gone ahead of the Church as though separated from her; rather, they have gone before us
corrections.corrected: Yet they are not cut off from the Church, because they have gone before us
corrections.latin: sed non praeceduntur ab Ecclesia, quia praecedunt cum signo fidei
corrections.reason: Printed 'praeceduntur' ('are preceded') yields no sense; it is evidently a misprint for 'praeciduntur' ('are cut off'), which makes the 'quia' clause coherent and matches Florus's 'Neque enim piorum animae mortuorum separantur ab Ecclesia' below. The English had rendered neither the passive nor 'quia'.

corrections.original: The phrase “sed non praeceduntur ab Ecclesia” is syntactically awkward; I have taken Florus to mean that the dead have gone before the living faithful, but not in separation from the Church.
corrections.corrected: Printed “sed non praeceduntur ab Ecclesia” (“they are not preceded by the Church”) is an evident misprint for “praeciduntur” and is translated “they are not cut off from the Church”.
corrections.latin: sed non praeceduntur ab Ecclesia
corrections.reason: name the misprint and replace the superseded note

corrections.original: the most courageous man and leader Judas
corrections.corrected: the most courageous man and high priest Judas
corrections.latin: vir fortissimus et pontifex Judas
corrections.reason: Florus calls Judas 'pontifex'; translate what he says. The historical point belongs in the note.

corrections.original: “Pontifex” is translated here as “leader,” since Judas Maccabeus was not high priest in the strict later sense.
corrections.corrected: Florus calls Judas “pontifex”, translated “high priest” as he wrote it; historically Judas Maccabeus did not hold the high priesthood.
corrections.latin: pontifex Judas
corrections.reason: replace the superseded note

corrections.original: by the power of his grace and with the help of the venerable sacrament
corrections.corrected: by his power and grace, and with the help of the venerable sacrament
corrections.latin: per virtutem et gratiam ejus Deus venerabilis sacramenti auxilio ad eamdem beatitudinem perducat
corrections.reason: 'virtutem et gratiam' are two nouns ('power and grace'), not 'the power of his grace'.

corrections.original: The Hebrews citation is printed as chapter five, verse one, but the quotation continues through material corresponding to verses two and three. The Latin opens a quotation before Gregory’s words and does not clearly close it; the translation treats the Gregory quotation as ending after “made us ourselves into a sacrifice,” where the sense changes back to Florus’s exposition.
corrections.corrected: The printed 'per virtutem et gratiam ejus Deus venerabilis sacramenti auxilio … perducat' is read with 'Deus' as the resumed subject ('that God … by his power and grace, and with the help of the venerable sacrament'); 'ejus Deus' may be a corruption of 'ejusdem' ('by the power and grace of that same venerable sacrament'), but this is uncertain.
corrections.latin: per virtutem et gratiam ejus Deus venerabilis sacramenti
corrections.reason: record uncertain reading

corrections.original: “Through whom you always create all these good things,”
corrections.corrected: “Through whom you always create all good things,”
corrections.latin: «Per quem omnia semper bona creas,» etc.
corrections.reason: Florus's lemma has no 'haec'; 'these' completes it from the familiar canon wording.

corrections.original: By sanctifying, he gives life,
corrections.corrected: And so, by sanctifying, he gives them life,
corrections.latin: ut quae erant simplex creatura, fiant sacramenta; sicque sanctificando vivificet
corrections.reason: 'sicque' (and so) was dropped, breaking the link with the preceding purpose clause.

corrections.original: in the Father, sourcehood is indicated to us
corrections.corrected: in the Father, authority is indicated to us
corrections.latin: Insinuatur itaque nobis in Patre auctoritas
corrections.reason: 'sourcehood' is a coinage that the voice would stumble over; 'authority' (auctoritas, in the sense of origin) is the standard rendering.

corrections.original: and the one who hears is the one who shows mercy.
corrections.corrected: but the one who shows mercy hears it with his ears.
corrections.latin: silentium est, clamat pectus, sed auribus ille audit qui miseretur
corrections.reason: 'auribus' and the contrast 'sed' were dropped; translated as printed.

corrections.corrected: “sed auribus ille audit qui miseretur” is translated as printed (“but the one who shows mercy hears it with his ears”); the printed text may be defective here (e.g. a lost negative or 'cordis'), but no emendation is made.
corrections.latin: sed auribus ille audit qui miseretur
corrections.reason: record possibly defective reading

corrections.original: We ask that, if we are deprived of his help, we may not consent to any temptation through deception, nor give way to it under pressure.
corrections.corrected: We ask that we may not be left without his help, and so be deceived into consenting to some temptation, or be overcome by affliction and give way to it.
corrections.latin: Petimus ne deserti ejus adjutorio, alicui tentationi vel consentiamus decepti, vel cedamus afflicti.
corrections.reason: Mistranslation: 'deserti ejus adjutorio' is part of what the petition fears (Augustine, Enchiridion 116). The English made desertion a granted condition and asked to resist without God's help, reversing the theology.

corrections.original: in every offering of the Lord’s day.
corrections.corrected: in every offering of the Lord.
corrections.latin: in omni Dominica oblatione
corrections.reason: 'Dominica oblatio' is the Lord's offering, the Eucharist (cf. §89 'Dominicam oblationem' = 'the Lord's offering'), not a Sunday offering.

corrections.original: And as far as inward peace is concerned,
corrections.corrected: And as far as outward peace is concerned,
corrections.latin: quantum vero ad interiorem pacem, simus etiam «ab omni perturbatione securi.»
corrections.reason: The second 'interiorem' is an evident misprint for 'exteriorem': the contrast is inward devotion (free from sins) against outward peace (safe from disturbance). Owner rule: translate the evident sense and note it.

corrections.original: Column marker omitted from the English as editorial apparatus.
corrections.corrected: The printed Latin has 'interiorem' twice ('quantum ad interiorem religionis devotionem … quantum vero ad interiorem pacem'); the second is an evident misprint for 'exteriorem' and is translated 'outward peace'.
corrections.latin: quantum vero ad interiorem pacem
corrections.reason: record evident misprint translated by sense

corrections.original: to whom we offer sacrifices together with the Father,
corrections.corrected: to whom, together with the Father, we offer sacrifices,
corrections.latin: cui cum Patre hostias offerimus
corrections.reason: Fulgentius: Christ, with the Father, receives the sacrifice. The old word order let a listener hear the Father offering alongside us.

corrections.original: is brought before us at the altar.
corrections.corrected: is renewed at the altar.
corrections.latin: cum ejusdem beatae passionis ad altare memoria replicatur
corrections.reason: 'replicatur' = repeated, renewed; the argument about daily sins depends on the repetition.

corrections.original: Therefore, in one saint all are equally honored, and in one saint all are equally neglected.
corrections.corrected: And they wish that in one of them all may be equally honored, and in one of them all equally slighted.
corrections.latin: et ut in uno omnes pariter habeantur, et in uno omnes pariter negligantur
corrections.reason: the ut-clause depends on 'desiderant et rogant' (a wish), not an independent statement

corrections.original: By love for this peace, as far as he grants it, we are set on fire.
corrections.corrected: By love for him, as far as he grants it, we are set on fire.
corrections.latin: et amore ipsius, quantum donat, accendimur
corrections.reason: ipsius refers to Christ, like 'in eum' just before
